lessonRef.subject: financial-literacy
lessonRef.title: Reteach and varied practice: fixed variable and periodic expenses

objective: Learners re-practise expense classification and periodic conversion, and check the resulting budget against invented income.
scenario: Beatrix is an invented eighth grader rebuilding a pretend budget: $1,200.00 of fixed costs, $480.00 of variable costs, and an invented $900.00 annual registration bill, against $1,900.00 of monthly income.
safetyNotes: Every amount, person, business, and account in this task is invented for practice. Nothing here refers to a real household.
Never write a real bank account, card, PIN, password, Social Security, or tax number on this sheet; the task never asks for one.
This is education, not individualized financial advice. Real money decisions belong to a trusted adult.

tasks.directions: Convert Beatrix's invented annual registration bill into a monthly equivalent.

prompts.text: What is the monthly equivalent of the $900.00 annual bill?

tasks.directions: Build Beatrix's full monthly cost from fixed, variable, and the periodic equivalent, then compare it with income.

prompts.text: What is the full monthly cost?
How much of the $1,900.00 income is left?

tasks.directions: Model the month Beatrix's registration bill actually lands with nothing set aside, and the effect of variable costs rising to $560.00.

prompts.text: What is the position in the bill month with nothing set aside?
With the periodic cost spread and variable costs at $560.00, how much is left?

tasks.directions: The margin was thin before anything went wrong.

prompts.text: Using Beatrix's figures, explain how much room the budget really has and what a single unplanned $200.00 cost would do to it.

remediation: If a learner mixes the spread and unspread versions, keep two clearly labelled scenarios for Beatrix and complete each separately.
extension: Ask the learner what variable-cost level would leave Beatrix exactly break-even with the periodic cost spread.
